samf-senior-1998-r2-01.title: Multiply the remaining fractions
samf-senior-1998-r2-01.body:
After the discounts the price is $0.9\times0.8=0.72$ of the original, so the single equivalent discount is $100\%-72\%=28\%$.

**Answer: (D) 28%**

samf-senior-1998-r2-02.title: Count
samf-senior-1998-r2-02.body:
The integers from $n$ to $m$ inclusive number $m-n+1$; removing the two endpoints leaves $m-n-1$. (Check: $m=5,n=2$: the integers 3, 4, i.e. 2 $=5-2-1$.)

**Answer: (B) $m-n-1$**

samf-senior-1998-r2-03.title: Volume of a cylinder
samf-senior-1998-r2-03.body:
Radius $=7.5$ mm $=0.75$ cm; length $=20$ m $=2000$ cm. Volume $=\pi(0.75)^2\cdot2000\approx3.14\cdot0.5625\cdot2000\approx3534$ cm$^3\approx3.5$ litres.

**Answer: (B) 3.5**

samf-senior-1998-r2-04.title: Scale factor
samf-senior-1998-r2-04.body:
The sides are in ratio $4:1$, so the areas are in ratio $4^2:1^2=16:1$.

**Answer: (D) 16:1**

samf-senior-1998-r2-05.title: Use the prime 5
samf-senior-1998-r2-05.body:
$6!=720=6\cdot5\cdot4\cdot3\cdot2\cdot1$ is divisible by 5, so one of $a,b$ is at least 5; and neither exceeds 5 (since $6!/6!=1$ would force the other to be 1). So one factor is $5!=120$ and the other is $720/120=6=3!$. Hence $\{a,b\}=\{3,5\}$ and $a+b=8$.

**Answer: (A) 8**

samf-senior-1998-r2-07.title: Similar right triangles
samf-senior-1998-r2-07.body:
Let $P$ be the vertex of the shaded rectangle on $DC$, with $DP=5$ and $PC=8$. The side of the shaded rectangle through $P$, extended, passes through $B$: right triangle $PCB$ has legs $PC=8$, $CB=6$ and hypotenuse $PB=10$. The side of the shaded rectangle through $D$ is parallel to $PB$, and the other side through $P$ is perpendicular to it; so the right triangle formed at $D$ with hypotenuse $DP=5$ is similar to triangle $BPC$ (ratio $\frac12$), with legs $4$ and $3$. Hence the shaded rectangle has one side $3$ (the distance between the parallel lines through $D$ and $P$). By the symmetry of the figure about the centre of $ABCD$, the part of $PB$ outside the shaded rectangle at the $B$ end also has length 4, so the other side is $PB-4=10-4=6$. Area $=3\times6=18$.

**Answer: (E) 18**

samf-senior-1998-r2-10.title: Tangent lengths
samf-senior-1998-r2-10.body:
Let $AY=AZ=z$, $BZ=BX=y$, $CX=CY=x$. Then $x+y=a$, $x+z=b$, $y+z=c$. Adding the last two and subtracting the first: $2z=b+c-a$, so $AY=z=\frac12(b+c-a)$.

**Answer: (C) $\frac12(b+c-a)$**

samf-senior-1998-r2-11.title: Isosceles triangle $ABH$
samf-senior-1998-r2-11.body:
Each interior angle of a regular octagon is $\frac{(8-2)\cdot180^\circ}8=135^\circ$. Triangle $ABH$ is isosceles with $AB=AH$ and apex angle $135^\circ$, so $\angle ABH=\frac{180^\circ-135^\circ}2=22\frac12^\circ$. Then $\angle HBC=\angle ABC-\angle ABH=135^\circ-22\frac12^\circ=112\frac12^\circ$.

**Answer: (A) $112\frac12^\circ$**

samf-senior-1998-r2-12.title: Count incidences
samf-senior-1998-r2-12.body:
Each of the 12 pentagons has 5 vertices and 5 edges. Three faces meet at each vertex, so $V=\frac{12\cdot5}3=20$. Each edge belongs to two faces, so $E=\frac{12\cdot5}2=30$. $V+E=50$.

**Answer: (C) 50**

samf-senior-1998-r2-12.title: Euler's formula
samf-senior-1998-r2-12.body:
$V-E+F=2$ with $F=12$ gives $V-E=-10$; with $E=30$ we get $V=20$ again. Sum $=50$.

**Answer: (C) 50**

samf-senior-1998-r2-13.title: Case analysis
samf-senior-1998-r2-13.body:
Agnes and Billy contradict each other, so exactly one of them tells the truth (on this occasion). Hence 'Agnes and Billy are both lying' is false, so Charlotte lies. If Agnes were truthful, Billy would always speak the truth, so 'Agnes is lying' would be true: contradiction. So Agnes is lying and Billy's statement is true. Only Billy speaks the truth.

**Answer: (B) Only Billy**

samf-senior-1998-r2-14.title: Divisibility
samf-senior-1998-r2-14.body:
The left side $6x+15y=3(2x+5y)$ is a multiple of 3 for all integers $x,y$, but $85$ is not a multiple of 3. So there are no solutions.

**Answer: (A) 0**

samf-senior-1998-r2-15.title: Areas of the four triangles
samf-senior-1998-r2-15.body:
Triangles $AOD$ and $COB$ are similar, so $\dfrac{DO}{OB}=\dfrac{AO}{OC}$. Triangles with the same height have areas proportional to their bases: $\dfrac{DO}{OB}=\dfrac{[AOD]}{[AOB]}$ and $\dfrac{AO}{OC}=\dfrac{[AOB]}{[BOC]}$. Hence $\dfrac x{[AOB]}=\dfrac{[AOB]}y$, so $[AOB]=\sqrt{xy}$, and similarly $[DOC]=\sqrt{xy}$. The trapezium has area $x+y+2\sqrt{xy}=(\sqrt x+\sqrt y)^2$.

**Answer: (D) $(\sqrt x+\sqrt y)^2$**

samf-senior-1998-r2-16.title: Split into odd and even denominators
samf-senior-1998-r2-16.body:
Let $t=1+\frac1{3^2}+\frac1{5^2}+\cdots$ (reciprocals of odd squares). The even-denominator terms are $\frac1{2^2}+\frac1{4^2}+\cdots=\frac14\left(1+\frac1{2^2}+\frac1{3^2}+\cdots\right)=\frac14s$. Since $s$ is the sum of both kinds of terms, $s=t+\frac14s$, so $t=\frac34s$.

**Answer: (B) $\frac34s$**

samf-senior-1998-r2-19.title: Arrangements with repeats
samf-senior-1998-r2-19.body:
The notes are C, C, G, G, G, A, A: C twice, G three times and A twice. The number of distinct arrangements is $\dfrac{7!}{2!\,3!\,2!}=\dfrac{5040}{24}=210$.

**Answer: (B) 210**
